method: Per-unit 3a implementer simulation over every file in full, 3b rubric scoring against pipeline-rubrics/references/vision-rubric.md with file:line evidence, 3c hostile re-read of both scores and findings. Rubric scores follow the rubric rows literally; cross-reference-integrity defects are reported as findings under their nearest dimension without inflating a rubric row the criteria do not describe.

findings.claim: Whether point-of-sale screening produces a match on a partial identity key is stated three mutually incompatible ways — within one file and across two — so an implementer must invent the matching rule that governs the domain's self-declared worst output.
findings.evidence: 15.02.02-point-of-sale-serial-screening.md:67 (States table) — "| Partial | Identity partially resolved (no era, no serial) | \"Limited check — we matched on maker and model only\" |". Contradicted by the same file at :54 — "| Serial-less gear (15.01.05) | Screening cannot match | \"This gear has no serial — we can't check it against the registry\" — stated plainly rather than showing a hollow green tick |", and by 15.02.01-theft-report-serial-flagging.md:50 — "| Serial unknown | Flag on `(maker, model, era, ?)` — a partial key | Flag exists but cannot support point-of-sale screening (needs full composite key per parent D-02); honest that it is close to useless for matching until the serial is added |". The parent decision's rationale forbids the loosest reading outright: 15.02-stolen-gear-registry-recovery-index.md:51 D-02 — "Screening keys on the composite identity `(maker, model, era, serial)` ... A false 'stolen' on a listing is the worst output this domain can produce — it defames a seller and kills a legitimate sale."
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must decide whether a maker+model-only match is emitted at all, and if so what it renders as. Choosing the States-table reading flags every Les Paul of a model whose sibling was stolen — precisely the defamation outcome D-02 exists to prevent; choosing the other two readings means the documented Partial state is unreachable and its user-facing string is dead.
findings.failureScenario: A flag is filed with an unknown serial on a stolen 1959 Les Paul. An honest seller lists a different 1959 Les Paul. Implementer A (States table) shows "Limited check — we matched on maker and model only" and surfaces a stolen-registry match on the innocent listing; implementer B (:54 and 15.02.01:50) shows no check at all. Same spec, opposite legal exposure.

findings.claim: The canonical identity-confidence value set is absent from the file that two ratified decisions name as its author, while the only enumeration on disk sits in the file those decisions forbid from defining one — so there is no authoritative vocabulary to build against.
findings.evidence: 15.01.05-non-serialized-contested-identity.md:93 D-03 — "**DQ-MG-05:** this file **authors** the canonical identity-confidence value set; `15.01.01` renders it and never defines its own ... The values are the six already in use on disk; relocating them costs nothing because no downstream literal binds to them today." No enumeration follows anywhere in that file (a full-text scan of 15.01.05 finds only two incidental value mentions, `photo-bound` at :45 and `era-unknown` at :57). The six values exist only in 15.01.01-gear-record-serial-identity.md:87-95 (`serial-confirmed`, `serial-typed`, `serial-reconstructed`, `photo-bound (no serial)`, `era-unknown`, `numbers-disagree`), which then says at :96-98 — "15.01.05 owns resolution logic and the authoritative value set; this feature owns the render and the record's behaviour at each level. The vocabulary above is proposed from the render side and is flagged for Step 6 synthesis against 15.01.05's." The relocation is also ratified platform-wide at ideation-index.md:250 D-65 — "`15.01.05` authors the canonical confidence set and `15.01.01` renders it".
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must either adopt the enum from the file that is explicitly barred from defining it (violating D-03/D-65), or invent 15.01.05's set from prose. The instruction to synthesise "against 15.01.05's" set cannot be executed because no such set exists, and the deferral names an internal step rather than an owner and a pipeline stage.
findings.failureScenario: Two implementers write the identity-confidence contract. One binds to 15.01.01's six literals; the other, reading D-03 and D-65, treats 15.01.05 as authoritative, finds nothing, and derives a different set from its prose (e.g. collapsing `serial-typed` and `serial-reconstructed`, which 15.01.01 D-07 and DT-05 require to be distinct because the post-theft registrant's record must be legible as reconstructed).

findings.claim: The domain CX file states that theft-report standing is unresolved and cites a question number that covers something else, contradicting the ratified decision recorded in three other places.
findings.evidence: gear-registry-ownership-cx.md:228 — "When owner and holder differ, both may file, but standing rules are unresolved (Q-04)." and :239 — "**Permission intersection**: Who has standing to file? Unresolved — 15.08 Q-01. The holder notices; the owner has standing; both may need to." Both are false as of the ratified record: 15.08-custody-loans-consignment.md:114 Q-01 — "**RESOLVED (D-64 / DQ-MG-04, ratified 2026-07-21)** — **both**, bounded: *\"The owner or a party in a `15.08` custody state may file, with capacity recorded; the platform never adjudicates title.\"*"; 15.02.01-theft-report-serial-flagging.md:99 Q-01 — "**Resolved by DQ-MG-04 / D-05 (2026-07-21)**"; ideation-index.md:249 D-64. The cited "(Q-04)" also points at the wrong row — 15.02-stolen-gear-registry-recovery-index.md:62 Q-04 is about flagging unregistered gear and says of itself "DQ-MG-04 additionally records that this row *\"is not standing authority\"* — who may file is 15.02.01 Q-01."
findings.forcedInvention: An implementer reading the domain cross-cut before the leaves would treat filing standing as an open product decision and either block holder-filed reports or invent an eligibility rule, instead of implementing the enumerated-custody-state rule already ratified.
findings.failureScenario: The theft-report gate is built owner-only because the domain CX says standing is unresolved. A studio engineer who discovers a session player's guitar is gone — the case D-64 exists to serve — cannot file, and the report waits weeks for an owner who does not know yet.

findings.claim: The domain index's structural summary contradicts the tree it maps and its own MoSCoW table on three separate counts, all unmarked.
findings.evidence: gear-registry-ownership-index.md:28-29 — "> 10 children classified through the Node Classification Gate: **5 sub-domains** (folders with index + CX) and **5 features** (leaf files). 21 leaf features total. All `[SURFACE]` pending Step 5 deepening." On disk there are 24 leaf features (15.01×6 + 15.02×4 + 15.05×3 + 15.06×3 + 15.07×3 + five flat features), which the same file's own MoSCoW table enumerates exactly (:105-107 lists 1 Must + 10 Should + 13 Could = 24) and which the root index confirms — ideation-index.md:132 "| 15 | Gear Registry & Ownership | ... | 5 sub-domains + 24 features |". The "All `[SURFACE]`" claim is contradicted by the Status column three lines below (five children read `[BREADTH]`) and by the files themselves (15.01.01 is `[DEEP]`, seven leaves are `[PARTIAL]`). The cross-cut summary is also wrong: index:48 — "10 confirmed pairs, 5 rejected, 5 mechanisms escalated" versus gear-registry-ownership-cx.md:5 — "19 intra-domain cross-cuts synthesised, 6 pairs rejected, 5 mechanisms escalated" and 19 CX rows plus R-01..R-06 actually present.
findings.forcedInvention: Anyone sizing or sequencing this domain from its index (which the pipeline designates the entry point) plans against 21 leaves, 10 cross-cuts and a uniformly un-deepened tree, and must reconcile three numbers by hand before trusting any of them.
findings.failureScenario: A downstream planner enumerates decomposition work from the index summary, omits three leaf features and nine cross-cuts, and treats already-deepened content as pending.

findings.claim: Seven `#CX-NN` anchors in this unit resolve to unrelated cross-cuts in the current domain CX numbering, sending a reader to the wrong relationship.
findings.evidence: 15.03-service-repair-modification-history.md:56 — "Routed to 15.05.01; see `#CX-04`" and :82 — "Triggers revaluation in **15.05.01 Automated Valuation** ... — see `#CX-04`", but gear-registry-ownership-cx.md:29 CX-04 is "Identity & Provenance ↔ Custody"; the Service↔Valuation pair is CX-10 (:35). 15.04-gear-collection-visibility.md:86 — "see gear-registry-ownership-cx.md`#CX-07`, the domain's most important cross-cut", but CX-07 (:32) is "Stolen Registry ↔ Valuation & Insurance"; the exposure hazard so described is CX-06 (:31, titled "THE EXPOSURE HAZARD"). Same error at gear-registry-ownership-index.md:128 Q-05 ("a targeting package for endemic gear theft (CX-07)") and 15.09-gear-discography.md:74 ("cannot un-widen a fact the session already published (CX-07)" — the collection-vs-credit tension is CX-14, :39). 15.08-custody-loans-consignment.md:93 — "Determines standing in **15.02.01 Theft Report** ... see `#CX-05`" (Stolen↔Custody is CX-08, :33; CX-05 is Identity↔Discography) and :94 — "Required by **15.06.01 Rig Definition** and **15.07.01 Org Asset Register** — see `#CX-06`" (those are CX-15 and CX-18). 15.10-cases-manifests-carnet-source-data.md:81 — "Many-to-many with **15.06.01 Rig Definition** — see ... `#CX-09`" (rig↔cases is CX-16; CX-09 is Stolen↔Cases). The CX file itself acknowledges a renumbering at :161 — "(see CX-08 in the old numbering ...)".
findings.forcedInvention: Nothing behavioural, but every one of these is the pointer the reader is told to follow for the coupling's synthesis detail, and each lands on a different pair whose synthesis answers different questions.
findings.failureScenario: An implementer following 15.08's pointer for theft-report standing reads CX-05's discography synthesis, finds nothing about standing, and concludes the coupling is unspecified.

findings.claim: A disputed gear-discography link is specified both as suppressed from public surfaces and as rendered honestly-as-disputed on the provenance chain; the two cannot both hold and neither is marked.
findings.evidence: 15.09-gear-discography.md:120 D-05 — "The link inherits the credit's *status*, not only its visibility: a disputed credit yields a suppressed link, failing safe toward non-disclosure", reinforced at :71 ("Public surfaces show nothing for that link until the dispute resolves") and :86 ("Only visible, undisputed links shown"). Against gear-registry-ownership-cx.md:164 (CX-05 synthesis 5) — "A disputed credit (domain 02) changes a chain fact — the chain renders the disputed state honestly, never as clean." 15.01.04-provenance-chain-view.md:82 confirms the chain renders 15.09's events, and its sibling treatment of contested facts is the opposite of suppression (:54 "a contested flag renders as contested, never as 'stolen'"; :57 "event kept, confidence for that link reduced, never silently removed").
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must choose whether the chain shows a disputed-session marker or nothing at all for a suppressed link — a visible product behaviour on the passport a buyer reads, with domain D-06 ("the registry never overstates what it knows") arguing for the marker and 15.09 D-05's fail-safe arguing for the omission.
findings.failureScenario: Implementer A renders "Played on: [record] — disputed" on a public passport, disclosing a contested session credit 15.09 DT-01 treats as a confidentiality leak. Implementer B omits the link entirely, producing a chain that reads clean about a fact the platform knows is contested.

findings.claim: A `held`-minted record is declared unlistable by the holder, while the custody feature's ratified decision authorises exactly that holder to list on granted selling rights — the consignment case both files call central.
findings.evidence: 15.01.01-gear-record-serial-identity.md:47 (mint-intent table) — "| `held` | ... | Record + a **custody** record (15.08); **no claim** | Appears in the holder's register (15.07) / rig (15.06) / manifest (15.10). **Cannot be listed**, insured, transferred or valued by the holder |". Against 15.08-custody-loans-consignment.md:105 D-02 — "Listing rights derive from custody + granted selling rights, not from ownership alone | Per DT-03. Ownership-only blocks legitimate consignment; possession-only licenses theft", with :86 DT-03 — "**consignment is custody with selling rights** ... 'held with selling rights granted by the owner' is the state that authorises a listing, and it is neither ownership nor mere possession", and :34 enumerating "**Consignment** — a dealer holds it to sell it. Interacts with domain 13: who may list it?". 15.01.01:197 names the same dealer as the `held` path's archetype — "The `held` mint intent is the entry point for a dealer/studio/tech registering gear they hold but do not own".
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer building the listing gate must decide whether `held` is a permanent listing bar or a default that a recorded owner grant lifts — and, if the latter, whether a grant can exist on a record that carries no claim at all.
findings.failureScenario: A consignment dealer mints `held` for stock a client left with them. Implementer A blocks the listing forever (15.01.01:47), breaking the consignment flow 15.08 D-02 was written to enable; implementer B allows it on a self-asserted grant, which 15.08 D-04 says carries no rights.

findings.claim: An edge row states that the shared-serial discriminator is deferred, while the question it cites is recorded as resolved in the same file.

findings.claim: The theft-report file's custody edge row declares standing deferred while its own Q-01 declares it resolved, so the file contradicts itself about whether a core permission rule is settled.
findings.evidence: 15.02.01-theft-report-serial-flagging.md:51 — "| Stolen gear was under someone else's custody (15.08) | Both the owner and the holder may file ... | Flag goes live either way; a second filer on the same identity is folded into the existing flag, not a duplicate. **Final standing rules deferred — see Q-01 and 15.08 Q-01.** |". Against :99 Q-01 in the same file — "~~Who has standing to file when ownership and custody differ?~~ **Resolved by DQ-MG-04 / D-05 (2026-07-21):** the owner **or** a party in a custody state `15.08` already enumerates may file, with filing capacity recorded on the flag ... | Owner | ✅ `/ideate-validate`, 2026-07-21". The genuine residue is narrower and is stated only in 15.08:114 ("Standing under `stale` and `disputed` custody remains open"), which carries no owner or deferral target of its own.
findings.forcedInvention: The implementer must decide whether standing is implementable now (per Q-01) or blocked (per the edge row), and specifically whether a holder under `stale` or `disputed` custody — two states 15.08's own States table defines — may file. Nothing in the tree assigns that residue an owner or a stage.
findings.failureScenario: A borrowed amp's custody has gone `stale` (no confirmation in 90+ days) when the holder discovers it stolen. One implementer accepts the filing under the enumerated-state rule; another rejects it because `stale` is not one of the six custody reasons and the standing residue is undocumented.

findings.claim: The sub-domain CX defers two items to a completed pipeline stage, one of them a question the leaf file records as resolved.
findings.evidence: 15.02-stolen-gear-registry-recovery-cx.md:57 — "An insurance payout (15.05.03) transfers ownership to the insurer in most policies — which should *change* the flag rather than clear it ... `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`", although 15.02.01-theft-report-serial-flagging.md:101 Q-03 records it "**Resolved (2026-07-23): the flag survives the payout and is never cleared ... the claimant identity under the flag is reassigned owner → insurer", with the only residue routed to `/write-be-spec` at 15.02.04-false-flag-dispute-lifecycle.md:96. Also :105 — "**State transition conflict**: A flag contested mid-checkout. The purchase and the state change can race. `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`", although 15.02.02-point-of-sale-serial-screening.md:56-57 specifies both mid-checkout races in full ("it runs at payment commit, inside the same transaction that mints the witnessed transfer (15.01.03)" and "checkout pauses on an interstitial requiring explicit re-confirmation").
